summary: OpenAI published a field report of eight case studies where research teams used Codex (and in some cases Claude Code) coding agents to modernize, optimize, and maintain scientific software in genomics and other data-rich fields, and summarized recurring lessons about validation and stewardship.

practices.reason: The report gives a concrete, transferable pattern for validating AI-agent-generated scientific code using external references and measurable acceptance targets, which an engineering team could apply directly.
practices.quote: The strongest approaches used an external reference or measurable acceptance target such as exact output agreement, parity with an existing tool, appropriate statistical behavior, or answers established in advance using simulated data.

practices.reason: The report describes a staged, feedback-driven workflow pattern for directing coding agents on complex projects, but the method is described at a case-study level rather than as a fully specified reusable procedure.
practices.quote: Contributors broke down broad goals into smaller changes, then used intermediate benchmarks and test systems to evaluate and refine the agents’ work.
